source_text: Dixi custodiam vias meas ut non delinquam in lingua mea. Posui ori meo custodiam cum consisteret peccator adversum me. Obmutui et humiliatus sum.
orientation: The psalmist speaks in the first person, resolving to guard his ways and his mouth while a sinner stands against him.
pass_a_gloss: I said I will guard my ways [so] that [I] may not offend in my tongue. I placed [a] guard [on] my mouth when [the] sinner stood against me. I was silent and [I] was humbled.

choices.why: Keeps the literal future force of the psalmist's resolution and the plain sense of viae as ways or paths.

choices.term: ut non delinquam in lingua mea
choices.english: so that I do not sin with my tongue
choices.why: Preserves the purpose clause and the literal 'in my tongue' as 'with my tongue' for natural English.
rejected: that I may not offend with my tongue
so as not to sin in my tongue

choices.english: I set a guard on my mouth
choices.why: Literal rendering of posui with custodiam as a noun, matching the psalm's image of placing a guard.
rejected: I placed a watch before my mouth
I put a muzzle on my mouth

choices.english: when the sinner stood against me
choices.why: Keeps the temporal cum clause and the literal stance of the sinner opposing the speaker.
rejected: while the sinner stood before me
as the sinner took his stand against me

choices.english: I was silenced and I was humbled
choices.why: Renders both passive forms literally, preserving the psalmist's passive suffering.
rejected: I was dumb and brought low
I kept silence and was humbled

bible_refs.note: Dixi custodiam vias meas ut non delinquam in lingua mea. Posui ori meo custodiam cum consisteret peccator adversum me. Obmutui et humiliatus sum.

pass_b_english: I said, “I will guard my ways so that I do not sin with my tongue.” I set a guard on my mouth when the sinner stood against me. I was silenced and I was humbled (Psalm 39:1, LXX 38:2).

last_rejected.source_quote: Dixi custodiam vias meas ut non delinquam in lingua mea. Posui ori meo custodiam cum consisteret peccator adversum me. Obmutui et humiliatus sum.
last_rejected.why: Citation format violates brief: should be Hebrew number with LXX note, not LXX number first.
last_rejected.ruling: Citation gives both Hebrew/Vulgate and LXX numbers correctly; format preference is not a major meaning-changing error.
